F2: The async legacy calls only record an error boolean in a histogram and never log the error, so a failed legacy write leaves no log line.
F3: Verified: lines 45 and 129 record storage failures in the legacy histogram, and line 166 records the legacy DeleteCollection in the storage histogram, so the metrics are wrong.
F4: Line 106 passes `name` as the `kind` label, which gives the metric unbounded cardinality and wrong data in newly written code.
F5: In mode 3, storage is the read authority, so returning NotFound is a reasonable simplification; the orphaned-legacy-row case is speculative.
F6: Legacy now re-applies the raw `objInfo` to its own old object instead of persisting the object storage wrote (unlike mode 2's `updateWrapper`), so the two stores can diverge.
F7: The finding itself says the dry-run handling predates this change; the old code also passed `options` to legacy unconditionally.
